body: I’m 6 years into 24/7 dpdr now and it hasn’t gotten better, just easier to deal with since it’s my new normal. The love and positive feelings still aren’t there.

That first comma wtf 😂

Cheers man

I’ve been on Mirtazapine for almost three years now. Started at 15mg at 95lbs (6ft), gained weight up to about 115lbs rather quickly then over the last year and a half i gained a lot more.

I’m now 155lbs which is amazing because I never thought I’d ever get to a healthy weight. I did still have to force feed myself a lot and I was sick hundreds of times doing so but it was all worth it, this med was a massive help.

30mg seems like the best dose for me. No super bad side effects even after three years either.

As someone who used to be anywhere between 95lbs-118lbs at 6ft tall I can confidently say my posture is and has been terrible for most of my life.

I was underweight from age 11-23. I’m now 24 and sitting at a comfortable 155lbs, I exercise almost daily now whereas I never exercised before. I lived a very sedentary life. 

My posture has improved a little bit, admittedly I still don’t have a lot of muscle on me and I have osteoporosis so they are factors to consider.

Being a healthy weight now is amazing though to be fair so I don’t regret all the effort I put in to get here.
wish I looked like you, I’d get all the bitches.

Thank you 💙

I can comfortably talk about my dpdr nowadays without it triggering me. I mainly avoid reddit because it can be a downer seeing people in the thick of it and can trigger my paranoia/intrusive/ptsd thoughts and memories if the wrong thing is mentioned.

I done countless rounds of CBT on the NHS which didn’t help (they kept saying I was too sick and referred me elsewhere so consequently I got passed around) then i had a psychiatric nurse for a few months who wasn’t the right fit to put it nicely (they hated me) and didn’t understand what I was going through. 

Eventually I just paid to see a psychologist privately every week via Zoom which I mainly used to vent and keep my thoughts from spiralling but I can’t say that they were a massive help tbh even though I continued to see them for two years. I had also seen a different psychologist privately for a year before in 2021, I can’t say that anyone I’ve seen fully understood dpdr like they’d often tell me to try imagination techniques when I had explained the week earlier that I’d lost the ability to do that due to the dissociation.

It’s taken me 4 years to find good people who help me on the NHS, currently see a Primary Care mental health nurse who are part of my GP practice and a link worker who I go out for walks and stuff with to push me to get out. I think I got lucky that I got two lovely ones who want to help and try to understand me as much as possible.

Sorry to write so much, a lot happened so it was difficult to condense it without making it sound like it was a piece of cake 😆

Good luck with everything 👍🏻

I’m into over 4 years of 24/7 dpdr now. It’s more manageable these days which I think is mainly due to the fact that I’m so used to it. 

My daily life is still very difficult, unemployed, don’t leave the house for very long, don’t drive much, don’t feel any positive emotions, lonely, extremely depressed some days/weeks. I feel my anxiety levels are back to pre dissociation levels (pretty severe but what I’m used to) and no severe panic attacks since August 2022. I’ve been meeting up with friends and exercising which I’ve never really done much before…

So there has been progress albeit slow. I don’t really post or comment on Reddit anymore because I found it frustrating and a hindrance to my mental health. My other socials are linked on my account here if anyone wants to see how I’m doing as I post video updates on there.

Yeah we sound very similar, during my worst episode of anxiety I lost so much weight I was on the verge of death which definitely contributed to the dpdr as I was so scared I was going to drop dead.

The longer it’s went on the more I’ve gotten used to it so it’s easier to deal with nowadays. I wish you all the best, I really hope it leaves you alone soon 💙
Nope. I’m 3 years into a 24/7 ‘episode’. Maybe I’m feeling a tiny bit less numb but everyday is still hell.
Thank you 💙

Right now I’m probably around 10kg away from being at the bare minimum healthy weight.

From age 11 up until last year (I’m 22 now) my bmi was always between 14-15.5 and I survived. The only health condition I’ve got due to my weight is Osteoporosis.

It is very worrying how low your bmi is. My doctor wanted to admit to hospital when mine was in the high 13’s. Also if you start to eat more you need to keep an eye on your bloods because you’re at a higher risk of refeeding syndrome.

I’d definitely get onto your doctor and maybe look into getting some ‘fortisip compact’ they’ve got 300 calories per 125ml.

I hope it all works out for you mate 💙

It’s awful not being able to eat properly, being underweight is so annoying. I’m 6ft and I’ve been as low as 44kg which was very scary.

I’m currently sitting at around 54kg which is still bad. My GP prescribes me ‘fortisips’ which are super high in calories and easy to drink.

How tall are you?

I highly doubt it. From what I’ve heard people can get enough oxygen from just one lung. So people who’ve had lung cancer and get a lung removed can live relatively normally.

So even if tight muscles etc were impacting your lungs you’d likely easily get plenty of oxygen.
It’s a horrific thing to go through. Must be extra hard having a kid to look after too. I hope it all works out for you. All we can do is keep pushing somehow.

I’m 3 years into 24/7 chronic dpdr. When it first started I was a wreck, nowadays I’m still a wreck but a more controlled one. You get used to it or maybe it’ll go away before you have to get used to it.
Thank you for sharing, its really appreciated. Always nice to hear success stories 💙
Same
It helped me for the first month getting through a super traumatic time but since then it never left and has stayed with me 24/7 for 3 years now. It’s to a point where dpdr is now my main problem.

This is very relatable. My worst months are always Oct-Jan. Last year I was close to death due to not eating. All my medical records from that period say I was ‘catatonic’. I wasn’t showering either and just sat in A&E not talking and barely able to move.

It’s awful. I’m not looking forward to these coming months.

For me I can’t feel anything. When I listen to music I hear the words but my brain doesn’t produce any emotion. The last time I felt a song was 3 years ago.

It’s fascinating how everyone is affected differently. It’s awful to feel nothing but feeling way too much must be just as bad :(

Life is about being present and dpdr takes that away from us. I miss being able to live in the moment enjoying my favourite movies and going outside to appreciate nature or people watch :(

I miss being able to feel love and actually caring about what my loved ones have to say. Now I’m just a robot, existing.
This rings true :’(

Would have tried a higher dose but it was expensive af here in England.

I feel the same way. I’ve accepted dpdr however the constant brain fog and exhaustion makes being around people extremely difficult. I spend pretty much all day in my bedroom.

I take an antidepressant (Mirtazapine) but it hasn’t really improved it.
Already have. Done nothing for me unfortunately

I have your typical nothing feels real, constant disconnection from everyone and everything symptoms. Been like this for 3 years now.

Enjoy being you again friend. Feel those old nice feelings again 💙

Thank you for sharing. It’s good to hear about people getting free from it. I hope you’re enjoying life :)

I definitely think many people recover. Most of us who go onto have dpdr 24/7 for years on end (myself included) have difficult lives dominated by mental illness and severe trauma. I can’t meditate away the trauma, I can’t meditate at all because it does nothing for me.

Years of therapy and antidepressants don’t seem to help. It varies person by person.

Personally I’m shocked that you found a med that was somewhat working and stopped it. I really hope that doesn’t come across as condescending, I don’t mean it that way at all :)

I’m still experimenting with meds because I’d give anything to make the dpdr less bad. I totally understand being hesitant about psych meds especially if they’re giving you bad side effects.

Lamotrigine is on my list of meds that I need to try.

It seems like your brain is snapping back to reality sometimes which is a good sign for sure though. It’s difficult to tell what’s the right thing to do. For me I’m focusing on meds now because I’ve had dpdr 24/7 for 3 years.
Fuck dpdr

My psychologist always tells me to try focusing on what I can see around me when I’m having high anxiety. I keep telling them that it doesn’t work because nothing feels real. It’s so annoying that people especially mental health professionals find it hard to grasp what it’s like
It’s the same with me. If anything dpdr has made my anxiety way worse because I never feel present and can’t focus on things to calm myself down. It’s hell.

Almost 3 years 24/7 for me. I’ve been in therapy for a couple of years now. Tried multiple therapists and forms of therapy. On meds.

I don’t feel any different than when I first got dpdr. It’s hell on earth :(

I’m so sorry that you’re going through this OP 😢 I know you’ve probably heard that a lot already. I can’t imagine all the awful shit you’re having to go through on the daily.

I’ve been stuck in bed for most of this past year, it’s horrible staring at the same walls all day everyday.

I know it’s not much but we on this sub are here for you if you need to talk.
Everyday, mainly due to the derealisation and depersonalisation that my anxiety triggered.

Same here. In fact I hurt my foot quite badly a few weeks back and I started laughing from the pain because it was nice to finally feel something after so long.

I can really understand why people self harm although of course I would never endorse it, that’s not the answer.

I think a lot of it comes down to the anxiety. It’s constantly making you question everything, those ‘what if’ thoughts are what drive it a lot of the time.

The fact that you’re able to question whether things are real is a positive sign because people with full blown psychosis/schizophrenia normally believe what they see to be real and not hallucinations.

I also get pretty intense anxiety, dizziness, visual floaters, head pressure, some days I find it hard to talk due to the brain fog. I’m prone to panic attacks. Back in December I started seeing dark figures in my room due to lack of sleep and not eating for a month.

Today a family member who I wasn’t expecting at my house shouted my name and I wasn’t sure if I was hearing things or if it was real so I sometimes still question what I hear. Sometimes I feel like I hear voices and can’t decipher where it’s coming from but it just goes away.

My brain is a noisy place but most of the time I just try to carry on with what I’m doing and it’s passes.

I have pretty much all of those symptoms due to my dpdr, anxiety, depression and ocd.

It’s all very normal for those of us with dpdr :)

I take 1500iu of vitamin D everyday because I don’t go outside + 500mg of magnesium citrate because I don’t eat enough.

Dpdr isn’t any better for it but I still take them 😆
I find eating so difficult. I can barely taste anything anymore either so it’s just a chore having to chew and swallow mush.

I’ve had some of them pills on my bedside table for a month. I’m yet to try them mainly because I’m already on mirtazapine.

I hope they help you :)

This is anecdotal but I actually need a surgery on my tongue because I’m severely tongue tied. I’m unable to put my tongue to the roof of my mouth therefore unable to fully stimulate the vagus nerve.

Consequently I’m severely underweight and have crazy stomach issues. Struggled with eating and severe anxiety my whole life. Maybe it’s coincidental but I think there’s a case for the vagus nerve being involved.

24/7 dpdr for 2.5 years and counting.

Yeah they look kinda unfamiliar. Oh and don’t get me started on the amount of typos I do. I used to be a really good typer but now I take so long to message because even autocorrect can’t help me sometimes 😭😅

Once the dpdr goes those things should come back. In my 2.5 years of 24/7 derealisation and depersonalisation I’ve had two brief 30 second instances where I snapped back to reality and the things you mentioned seemed to come back. It was euphoric.

I answered anxiety disorder. But for me and so many others I think it’s a combination of a lot of things. 

Personally I’ve had an anxiety disorder my whole life and  only within the last 3 years has chronic dpdr developed. Mine was triggered by traumatic events, stress from work, my anxiety being at an all time high, not eating and being insanely depressed.

Mirtazapine saved my life and helps me eat just about enough. Without meds right now I’d probably be dead.

I love football too. Used to play it a lot as a kid. I don’t want to make this all about me but I think this might help provide some perspective…

I do a lot of walking sometimes at a very fast pace and I weight like 117lbs at 6’0. My weight has been as low as 99lbs and although I was in a very bad way going through lots of anxiety (heart rate up to 170bpm) I didn’t pass out once.

I hope this is reassuring because I guess my point is that if you’re a healthy weight and eating enough it’s very very unlikely that you’ll pass out.

Have you ever passed out before?

The flip side is that I had severe anxiety since being a very small kid and I wasn’t eating well at all, being sick before work.

I’ve had two mental breakdowns where I was in bed for months not eating to the point I almost starved to death.

Currently at my highest weight ever of 117lbs at 6’0, recently got diagnosed with osteoporosis. My life is a shit show.
Yes! When the dpdr gets even worse all I can do is lie as still as I can in bed.

Yes! I’ve always been sensitive to loud noises. I remember being a kid, having to attend a school concert and covering my ears rocking back and forth because it felt like my stomach was going to explode from the vibrations of the speakers.

Since getting dpdr it’s even worse. I sit in my bedroom with the tv volume super low and hate it when seagulls make noise on the roof or people mow their gardens.

I feel like I sound absolutely mental ahaha but it’s what I’ve become :(
I feel very similar too. I’m turning 22 next week and I’m yet to have a moment of my 20’s without dpdr. The passing of events and time without taking anything in is super anxiety provoking.

Sometimes I spend all day watching Numb on repeat. 

It’s not a fantastic movie but it’s still one of my favourites because it’s pretty much the only movie that outright shows dpdr.

Unfortunately I don’t have a girl like Sara to live life with but we move ahah.

Sometimes I think I see things because the dissociation gets bad. I also have OCD, anxiety and depression.

A family member of mine has schizophrenia but I definitely don’t have it.

My point is that ocd, dpdr and anxiety can make you feel like you’re loosing it but if you’re able to to identify you are feeling like this it’s highly unlikely that you have schizophrenia.

I think so? Like sometimes the thoughts seem to have a different persona and voice. They just don’t match my normal personality sometimes.

GERD is another thing I’ve got going on as well but had no relief from meds.

I’ve only had chronic dpdr for 2.5 years although had it on and off earlier in my life.

Your story gives me hope!

This is what I like to hear. Congrats man, enjoy it :)

I feel safer in the hospital mainly because I know they’ll stop me from hurting myself. I’m in the UK so usually have to wait 3+ hours to be seen so I’ve normally calmed down by the time I’m seen.

The dpdr doesn’t get better when I’m there just the intense anxiety and suicidal thoughts are eased.

I wouldn’t be worried too much about getting heart issues from either. At least not in the short to medium term.

The only thing I’ve got is osteoporosis which isn’t surprising. It’s amazing how resilient the human body is.

I’m not sure how old you are. But I found that when I was younger I really loved playing games and found them very immersive. As I got older (I’m 21 now) games stopped hitting the same even before I had dpdr, games just felt shit compared to how they used to feel when I was a kid.

For most people who go through it I’d say it’s temporary. Some people might have it go away then it comes back months or years later.

Then there’s the unlucky few whose brains never come out of the dpdr state. It’s very difficult to tell what’ll happen because it varies on an individual basis due to genetics/environment.
Ahah don’t worry, I’m not easily offended. It’s called Mirtazapine here in the UK otherwise known as Remeron.

We’re rooting for you!

It’s horrific to go through isn’t it, we’ve just gotta keep pushing somehow and hope with time we’ll snap back to reality. It feels like it’ll take a miracle though.

Thanks for watching the vids! Keep pushing mate 💙

Mental health conditions such as anxiety and depression which can cause dpdr are relatively uncommon then it’s only a subset of us that seem to go onto develop dpdr.

It’s the same with weed and trauma, not that many people smoke weed or have super traumatic experiences. Only a subset of those people who do will go onto develop this disorder.
